meaning: A thin, bendable disk in a plastic case that stored computer files. You carried it from one computer to another.
clues: Its tiny picture still stands for saving a file on many computers.
You could carry your files on it to another computer.
IBM began selling the first ones in 1971.
Installing one big program could take thirteen of them, fed in one at a time.
It has two words and ten letters in all, and the first word starts with F.

decoys.meaning: A stiff paper card with holes in set places. A machine read the holes as data.
A disk cartridge from 1994 that held 100 megabytes. That was far more than older small disks.
Reels of magnetic tape that stored computer data. They began replacing big stacks of punched cards in the early 1950s.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: I carried people's files between computers, and I kept spare copies safe. A second copy kept elsewhere is still smart.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Today's version: a USB stick. It's a small drive you plug in to carry files. Only plug in one you know, since a stray one can carry harmful software.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: And look, my picture is still the Save button. Not bad for an old fellow.
